page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7t.16xlarge is an x86_64 compute instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. Provisioned under the KVM hypervisor with dedicated CPU allocation, it features 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs via two threads per core. The instance provides 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining a standard general-purpose ratio of 4 GB per virtual core, alongside a baseline network throughput of 32 Gbps. The architecture incorporates advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI. It does not include integrated hardware accelerators or bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block volumes for non-volatile data persistence.

Benchmark results reveal strong multi-threaded execution metrics across diverse workloads. In stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core evaluations, the server ranks in the top 25% of tested systems, driven by its 64-thread parallelism. This parallel efficiency extends to compiling software with Clang, ray tracing, bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, and PassMark database operations, which all hit upper-quartile scores. Conversely, single-threaded throughput falls within the middle 50% tier, as reflected by average Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression metrics. System memory bandwidth also lands in the middle tier, delivering 170.68 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 69.67 GB/sec on uncached writes.

Because the platform trades top-tier single-core burst capability for dense multi-core parallel capacity, it offers qualitative resource efficiency for high-concurrency environments rather than latency-sensitive sequential tasks. The absence of local NVMe storage simplifies node replacements but mandates external storage planning for I/O operations. The server is well configured for enterprise backend services, distributed compilation jobs, large-scale container platforms, multi-threaded data processing, and relational database deployments using remote volumes.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7t.16xlarge is a dedicated x86_64 instance powered by a 32-core Intel Xeon 8369B processor executing across 64 vCPUs at 2.7 GHz. It integrates 256 GB of RAM, adhering to a 1:4 core-to-memory general-purpose ratio, and is supported by 32 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system includes AVX-512 VNNI and VAES cryptographic instruction sets, but includes neither integrated GPUs nor local disk storage. Benchmark testing highlights strong multi-core computational throughput, placing in the top quartile for Clang compilation, ray tracing, PassMark database processing, and parallel decompression. Single-core performance and memory bandwidth operate at average baseline levels. This profile makes the instance effective for concurrent containerized clusters, multi-threaded batch processing, backend application hosting, and distributed database services connected to networked block storage.
